authority_boundaries.awc: owns project and task identity, revisions, claims, leases, dependencies, and terminal commits
authority_boundaries.awr: owns enforcement of supplied bindings, opaque worktree allocation, routing, cleanup, and evidence projection
authority_boundaries.awq: owns quality acceptance and artifact evidence policy
authority_boundaries.awg: owns guidance and user-decision escalation; routing cannot decide

invariants: Every worktree is bound to exactly one tenant, project, task, revision, worker, lease, fence, and session.
AWR consumes an existing scheduler lease and never creates a competing lease authority.
A stale Coordinator revision or crossed dispatch lease is rejected before allocation.
Worktree keys are unique and collisions fail closed.
Opaque path tokens never expose a host path or permit path traversal.
Artifacts are namespaced by project and worktree.
Artifact content and provenance digests are immutable and replay-safe.
Artifact provenance retains the exact project revision and lease fence.
An artifact cannot be read by another project without an explicit dependency grant.
Dependency grants require both projects to exist and share a tenant.
Cross-tenant dependency grants and reads are always rejected.
Cleanup is fenced by the current worktree binding and is idempotent.
Interrupted cleanup remains pending and cannot be reported as complete.
Cleanup recovery requires a strictly newer lease fence.
Cleaned worktrees reject further artifact reads and writes.
Runtime routing cannot approve quality, guidance, specifications, tests, or terminal commits.
hostile_qualification: unknown project and malformed opaque binding
